sections.title: Policy and access
sections.text: Caldaro's parking questions revolve around the lake and the railway-station area. Traffic order 127/2026 of 27 July 2026 limits parking on the marked spaces north of the Mendelbahn valley station in St. Anton to 180 minutes with a parking disc, every day from 08:30 to 19:00, to ensure turnover; it follows an agreement between the provincial transport company STA and the municipality and takes effect once the signs are installed [0]. In a column of 21 August 2026 the mayor wrote that the Lido lease and the Lido car park are important income for the municipality, that lake access is free in the morning and evening, and that the free-access case, which the municipality won at first instance, is now before the Council of State; he asked where cars would park if access on the north shore were opened in haste [1]. A councillor said in June 2025 that visitors to the municipal Lido do not pay parking on top of entry, and that the former military site on the lake lacks water, electricity and parking [2]. The kindergarten and school street rules apply again from 7 September 2026, from 07:15 to 08:15 and from 12:40 to 13:10 [3]. A municipal mobility project started at the end of 2021 lists a mobility survey and cycling measures but no parking measures [14].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The main development is the Park & Ride at the station. On 11 September 2024 the province, the municipality and the Kellerei Kaltern signed an agreement for the redevelopment of the winery and station area and a new Park & Ride car park for commuters and Überetsch bus users, free for Südtirol Pass holders, with the bus parking to move to Kaltern Gand [11]. Salto reported that the station car park would cost about 3.8 million euros and the replacement bus park about 4.2 million euros, which was delayed; the council approved the restructuring plan on 12 September 2024 by majority, over opposition criticism, and no number of spaces was given [12]. On 2 October 2026 the municipality announced ground-breaking for the retail building in the same area; the release does not mention the car park or its schedule [13].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The Mendelbahn funicular has been run by the provincial company STA since 2021 and costs 13.50 euros return in autumn 2026 [8]. Regional tourism pages describe a large paid car park in front of the Lido and name a bus line to the lake, but give two different line numbers, 130 and 138, so we do not state which [7][9]. We found no current official tariff list.

Our data cover three car parks with 360 spaces from the South Tyrol open-data platform, measured since 27 September 2026: Trutsch open-air (140), Trutsch covered (150) and Maria Theresia (70). Occupancy averaged about 25% on weekdays and 22% at weekends, weighted by spaces, and no car park came close to full: the open-air Trutsch peaked at 75% on a Tuesday morning, the highest. This is about four weeks of data outside the bathing season, so the summer lake pressure the mayor describes is not visible in it.
